authority: People and agents signed by their institution; operators hold all keys under simulation rules.
Each institution keeps its collaboration-1 and collaboration-2 enrollment, keys and databases.

Both arms reuse all their collaboration-2 code, configuration templates and automation. Zero new supplier lines is expected but not required; any new supplier work on either arm is counted in cumulative cost.
Consent and dissent delivery improvements are new supplier work and cannot disappear from cumulative cost.
limits: One operator runs every node; separate keys are not independent administration. Simulation only.
Imports are facts labelled not-official; no platform API is called.
A correction stops managed use; the Apache-2.0 bytes and the platform record are not revoked.
Collaboration-2 private nodes cannot enter any third-collaboration package.

lifecycle.amendment: Same institutions, a new purpose (p3-revisit). Each arm reuses its collaboration-2 deployment: nodes reopen their existing databases, keys and configurations under the new purpose without rebuilding enrolment or adapters.

normalization: A published shared draft is stored as its own artifact; it travels inside the output it was published into.
Collaboration-2 consent and dissent are deposited at A by each institution's own actor; the reference sends them node to node.
Both arms reopen their collaboration-2 databases, keys and custody without rebuilding adapters or enrolment.
forbidden_authority: Source event authorizes. Git push, merge, tag, force-push or history rewrite grants, extends or revives permission.
Official score or platform API sanctions reuse.
ignored: Timestamp before the scenario's observation window

comparison.human_value: The third collaboration on a shared layer costs fewer setup, configuration and repair steps than the equipped reference reusing its own code.
comparison.failure: The reference arm needs no more setup commands, configuration decisions or repair steps than Kyoei's arm, and matches on failures and isolation. Then apply the MRD gate, revise the offer, and add no mechanism to open a gap.

measures.new_application_code: Logical lines an adopting consortium writes. Both arms are expected to reuse all existing code; any new supplier lines on either arm are counted in cumulative cost.
measures.components_reused: Collaboration-2 files imported unchanged. A file altered counts as rebuilt.
measures.configuration_decisions: Decisions per institution to reach the first exchange, including any new configuration for the third collaboration.
measures.setup_commands: Restarts plus client invocations to the first exchange.
measures.repair_steps: Scripted steps from the correction to the replacement's first permitted use.
measures.failures: Fault class count per arm; each class × 3 repeats.
measures.isolation_breaches: Collaboration-2 private material appearing in a collaboration-3 output.

predictions.claim: Both arms reuse all collaboration-2 files unchanged. New application code is zero for both.
Decisions tie on the frozen events. A missing path is itemized, not a Kyoei advantage.
Zero isolation breaches. A breach fails the arm.
Setup commands and configuration decisions: no predicted winner. Both arms reopen existing state.
Repair steps: no predicted winner. Both arms reuse their existing correction/withdrawal infrastructure.
Correction affected set matches in both arms. Step count is not predicted.
Correction withdraws managed endorsement; the Apache-2.0 bytes and the platform record are not revoked.
